name: Goblet Squat
purpose: The primary loaded squat pattern in this program because the front-loaded weight naturally teaches an upright torso and full-depth position.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against your chest with both hands, elbows tucked. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly. Sit down between your hips until your elbows lightly touch the inside of your knees, then drive back up through your whole foot.
form_cues: Keep the weight glued to your sternum
Push knees out in line with your toes
Keep heels down the whole rep
Chest tall, elbows point down not out
common_errors: Letting the weight drift away from the chest, tipping the torso forward
Heels lifting as depth increases
Knees caving inward on the way up
regressions: Bodyweight squat holding a post for balance
contraindications: reduce depth with acute knee pain

name: Dumbbell Front Squat
purpose: Allows heavier bilateral squat loading than a single goblet weight once the pattern is solid.
instructions: Clean two dumbbells to your shoulders and rest one end of each on the front of your shoulders, elbows lifted. Squat down under control until your thighs are at or below parallel, keeping your torso tall. Stand back up by driving the floor away, keeping the dumbbells stacked over your midfoot.
form_cues: Elbows up so the dumbbells sit on the shoulders, not the arms
Brace before you descend
Control down, drive up fast
Whole foot stays planted
common_errors: Letting the elbows drop so the arms hold the load and fatigue first
Rounding the upper back under heavier weight
Cutting depth as load increases
progressions: 1.5-rep front squat (bottom, halfway up, bottom, stand)
contraindications: avoid with acute wrist or anterior shoulder pain

name: Bodyweight Box Squat
purpose: A depth-controlled squat used for warm-ups, high-rep conditioning circuits, and as a reset when squat mechanics degrade.
instructions: Stand in front of a box or bench about knee height with feet shoulder-width apart. Reach your hips back and squat until you lightly touch the box, keeping your weight over your midfoot. Tap without fully sitting, then stand by squeezing your glutes at the top.
form_cues: Touch the box lightly, do not plop
Arms reach forward as a counterbalance
Shins stay fairly vertical as hips reach back
Stand fully tall between reps
common_errors: Collapsing onto the box and relaxing at the bottom
Looking down and rounding the back
Rocking forward off the box instead of driving through the feet

name: Kettlebell Deadlift
purpose: The entry-point hinge that grooves picking a load off the floor with a neutral spine before swings and heavier hinging.
instructions: Stand over a kettlebell with the handle roughly under your shoelaces. Push your hips back and bend your knees slightly until you can grip the handle with both hands and a flat back. Stand up by pushing the floor away and driving your hips forward, then reverse the motion to set it down.
form_cues: Hips back first, then bend the knees
Flat back from head to tailbone
Pull the slack out before you lift
Finish tall with glutes squeezed, not leaning back
common_errors: Squatting the weight up instead of hinging
Rounding the lower back to reach the handle
Hyperextending the lower back at lockout
regressions: Elevate the kettlebell on a box
Hip hinge drill with a dowel along the spine
contraindications: avoid during acute low back flare-up

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
purpose: Builds hamstring strength and hinge control through a long range of motion, the main posterior-chain strength lift of the block.
instructions: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart, knees softly bent. Push your hips straight back and slide the dumbbells down the front of your legs until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, usually around mid-shin. Drive your hips forward to stand, squeezing your glutes at the top.
form_cues: Hips travel back, not down
Dumbbells stay in contact with the legs
Soft knees, fixed knee angle throughout
Stop where the hamstrings stop, not where the floor is
common_errors: Bending the knees more as the weight lowers, turning it into a squat
Rounding the back to chase extra depth
Letting the dumbbells drift forward away from the legs
regressions: RDL to a box set at knee height
progressions: Heavier dumbbells with a 3-second lowering tempo
contraindications: avoid during acute low back flare-up

name: Kettlebell Swing
purpose: Develops explosive hip power and doubles as low-impact conditioning that pairs well with boxing rounds.
instructions: Start with the kettlebell about a foot in front of you, hinge and hike it back high between your thighs. Snap your hips forward to float the bell to roughly chest height, arms relaxed. Let it fall, hinge as the upper arms reconnect with your ribs, and repeat rhythmically.
form_cues: It is a hinge, not a squat
Hips drive the bell, arms just steer
Wait for the bell, then hinge late
Plank hard at the top: glutes and abs tight
common_errors: Lifting the bell with the arms and shoulders
Squatting under the bell instead of hinging
Hinging too early so the bell drops low and yanks the lower back
Leaning back at the top of the swing
contraindications: avoid during acute low back flare-up

name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
purpose: The most knee-friendly lunge variation, chosen as the main single-leg strength builder of the program.
instructions: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides. Step one foot back and lower until the back knee hovers just above the floor, front shin roughly vertical. Push through the front foot to return to standing, then repeat on the other side.
form_cues: Step back, drop straight down
Front knee tracks over the second toe
Torso tall with a slight forward lean from the hips
Push the floor away with the front foot
common_errors: Stepping too short so the front knee shoots far past the toes
Pushing off the back foot instead of the front leg
Wobbling from a tightrope-narrow stance
regressions: Bodyweight reverse lunge holding a wall or post
contraindications: shorten range with acute knee pain

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
purpose: The top-end single-leg strength progression, loading one leg heavily without heavy spinal loading.
instructions: Stand a couple of feet in front of a bench and place the top of your rear foot on it. Lower straight down until your front thigh is near parallel, keeping most of your weight on the front leg. Drive up through the front foot without bouncing off the back leg.
form_cues: Front foot far enough forward that the shin stays near vertical
Back leg is a kickstand, front leg does the work
Lower under control, no bouncing at the bottom
Square hips forward
common_errors: Standing too close to the bench, cramping the front knee
Loading the back leg and turning it into a quad stretch
Losing balance from a narrow base
regressions: Bodyweight split squat with hand support
progressions: Front-foot-elevated split squat for extra range
contraindications: avoid with acute knee pain
skip if balance issues make it unsafe

name: Lateral Lunge
purpose: Adds frontal-plane strength and adductor length, supporting hip mobility work and lateral movement in boxing footwork.
instructions: From a tall stance, step wide to one side and sit your hips back over the stepping leg, keeping the other leg straight with its foot flat. Lower until you feel a stretch along the inner thigh of the straight leg. Push off the bent leg to return to the start.
form_cues: Sit back into the hip, not down onto the knee
Both feet point mostly forward
Trailing leg stays straight with the foot flat
Chest up, back flat as hips reach back
common_errors: Bent knee caving inward
Heel of the working foot lifting
Rounding the spine to get lower instead of sitting back
contraindications: ease range with groin strain history

name: Push-Up
purpose: The baseline horizontal press, trains pressing and trunk stiffness together and scales anywhere without equipment.
instructions: Start in a straight-line plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders. Lower your whole body as one unit until your chest is about a fist's height from the floor, elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso. Press back up to a full lockout, pushing the floor away.
form_cues: Body moves as one rigid plank
Elbows about 45 degrees, not flared to 90
Chest leads, hips do not sag or pike
Full lockout with shoulder blades spreading at the top
common_errors: Hips sagging as reps fatigue
Half range: not reaching the bottom or the top
Head pecking forward while the chest stays high
Hands too far forward of the shoulders
contraindications: modify hand position with wrist pain

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
purpose: The main loaded horizontal press for building upper-body pushing strength beyond what push-ups provide.
instructions: Lie on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, feet planted on the floor. Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight over your mid-chest. Lower under control until the dumbbells reach the sides of your chest, then press again.
form_cues: Shoulder blades pinched down and back into the bench
Wrists stacked directly over elbows
Slight arch, ribs down, feet driving into the floor
Lower to a comfortable stretch, press to full lockout
common_errors: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides
Bouncing the dumbbells at the bottom
Feet dancing or lifting off the floor
Dumbbells drifting toward the face at lockout
regressions: Lighter dumbbells with a slow eccentric
contraindications: limit depth with anterior shoulder pain

name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up
purpose: Progresses the push-up by shifting load toward the upper chest and shoulders while demanding more trunk control.
instructions: Set your feet on a bench or box and hands on the floor in a plank position. Lower until your forehead is just above the floor, keeping the body in one line. Press back to full lockout without letting the hips pike.
form_cues: Squeeze glutes hard to keep hips level
Hands slightly ahead of the shoulders
Lower to the floor, not to a half rep
Tuck chin slightly so the head does not lead
common_errors: Piking the hips to make the rep easier
Cutting depth as the angle gets harder
Flaring elbows out wide
contraindications: avoid with acute shoulder impingement

name: Standing Dumbbell Overhead Press
purpose: The primary vertical press, building overhead strength while the standing position trains full-body bracing.
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward or slightly in, feet hip-width. Brace your trunk and press the dumbbells overhead until your biceps are near your ears and arms are locked out. Lower under control back to the shoulders.
form_cues: Squeeze glutes and abs so the ribs stay down
Press up and slightly back to finish over the shoulders
Wrists stacked over elbows the whole way
Head moves slightly through at lockout
common_errors: Leaning back and arching the lower back to press
Stopping short of full lockout
Flaring the wrists back under load
Using leg drive on strict reps
contraindications: avoid with acute shoulder impingement
modify with limited overhead mobility until t-spine work restores range

name: Pike Push-Up
purpose: A bodyweight vertical press for home sessions and a stepping stone toward more advanced overhead pressing.
instructions: From a push-up position, walk your feet in and lift your hips high so your torso points toward the floor like an inverted V. Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward a spot just in front of your hands. Press back up until your arms are straight, keeping hips high throughout.
form_cues: Hips stay high, torso as vertical as possible
Head travels forward of the hands, like a triangle
Elbows track back at about 45 degrees
Push the floor away until elbows fully straighten
common_errors: Letting the hips drop, turning it into a decline push-up
Lowering the head straight between the hands and jamming the wrists
Very short range of motion
regressions: Pike push-up with hands elevated on a box
contraindications: avoid with acute shoulder impingement
caution with wrist pain

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
purpose: The heaviest rowing option in the library, balancing all the pressing volume and building mid-back thickness.
instructions: Place one hand and the same-side knee on a bench, other foot planted, back flat and parallel to the floor. Row the dumbbell from a full hang up toward your hip, letting the elbow graze your ribs. Lower with control to a full stretch at the bottom.
form_cues: Pull the elbow to the hip, not the hand to the shoulder
Let the shoulder blade glide: reach at the bottom, squeeze at the top
Hips and shoulders stay square to the floor
Neck neutral, eyes on the bench
common_errors: Rotating the torso open to heave the weight up
Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear
Cutting the bottom stretch short
Jerking with momentum instead of pulling smoothly
progressions: Heavier dumbbell with a pause at the top

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
purpose: Rows with zero lower-back demand, isolating the upper back and enforcing strict technique on higher-volume days.
instructions: Set a bench to a low incline and lie chest-down on it with a dumbbell in each hand hanging straight down. Row both dumbbells up toward your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Lower slowly until your arms are fully extended and shoulder blades spread.
form_cues: Chest stays glued to the bench
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top
Full stretch at the bottom of every rep
Elbows track close to the body, about 45 degrees
common_errors: Lifting the chest off the bench to cheat the weight up
Short, choppy reps without full extension
Shrugging into the neck instead of pulling the blades back
progressions: Pause each rep at the top for 2 seconds

name: Standing Band Row
purpose: A joint-friendly, high-rep pulling option for warm-ups, home sessions, and posture work between pressing days.
instructions: Anchor a band at chest height and step back until there is tension with your arms extended. Pull the handles toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows behind you and squeezing your shoulder blades. Return slowly, letting your shoulder blades reach forward at the end.
form_cues: Stand tall, ribs stacked over hips
Lead the pull with the shoulder blades
Elbows finish just behind the torso
Resist the band on the way back out
common_errors: Leaning back with each rep to add fake range
Shrugging the shoulders up during the pull
Letting the band snap the arms back instead of controlling the return
regressions: Seated band row with legs extended
progressions: Single-arm band row with anti-rotation hold

name: Pull-Up
purpose: The benchmark vertical pull, a full-bodyweight strength standard this block trains directly and tracks over the four weeks.
instructions: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders, arms fully extended. Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down and back until your chin clears the bar. Lower under control to a full hang before the next rep.
form_cues: Start each rep from a dead hang
Pull the elbows down toward the ribs
Chest to bar, not chin poked over it
Ribs down, legs quiet, no swinging
common_errors: Kipping or swinging for momentum
Stopping with arms half bent at the bottom
Craning the neck to sneak the chin over
Losing body tension so the hips swing
regressions: Slow negative pull-ups (jump up, lower for 5 seconds)
progressions: Added weight via dumbbell between the feet
contraindications: avoid dead-hang starts with acute elbow tendinopathy

name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
purpose: Lets pull-ups be trained for full sets with clean form while strength builds toward more unassisted reps.
instructions: Loop a band over the bar and place one knee or foot in the loop. Perform pull-ups exactly as the unassisted version: dead hang start, chest toward the bar, controlled lowering. Choose the lightest band that still allows all planned reps with good form.
form_cues: Treat every rep like a real pull-up
Full hang at the bottom, chin clearly over at the top
Keep the banded leg steady so it does not bounce
Control the descent, do not ride the band down
common_errors: Using a heavier band than needed and stalling progress
Bouncing out of the bottom off band recoil
Shortening range at the top as sets fatigue

name: Kneeling Band Lat Pulldown
purpose: A high-rep vertical pull for lat volume and lat-engagement practice on days the bar is not available or arms are fried.
instructions: Anchor a band overhead, such as over the pull-up bar, and kneel below it holding the ends with arms extended overhead. Pull your elbows down and slightly back until your hands reach shoulder level, feeling the lats contract. Return slowly to a full overhead stretch.
form_cues: Pull elbows to the back pockets
Tall kneeling posture, ribs down
Feel the armpit muscles do the work
Slow stretch back to the top
common_errors: Leaning back and turning it into a row
Pulling with the hands and biceps only
Rushing the return and losing tension

name: Farmer's Carry
purpose: Trains grip, posture, and total-body work capacity in one drill and finishes sessions without beating up joints.
instructions: Deadlift a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell into each hand and stand tall. Walk with short, controlled steps for a set distance or time, keeping shoulders level and ribs stacked over hips. Set the weights down with a hinge, not a rounded back.
form_cues: Walk tall, as if a string pulls the crown of your head up
Crush the handles
Shoulders down and back, not shrugged
Smooth heel-to-toe steps, no waddling
common_errors: Leaning forward and rushing the steps
Letting the weights rest against the thighs
Rounding the back when picking up or setting down
regressions: Shorter carry distance with more sets

name: Suitcase Carry
purpose: A one-sided carry that hammers lateral core stability, directly supporting punching power transfer and single-leg work.
instructions: Pick up one heavy kettlebell or dumbbell in one hand and stand perfectly level, as if carrying a suitcase. Walk a set distance keeping your torso upright with no lean toward or away from the weight. Switch hands and repeat the same distance.
form_cues: Stay so level no one could tell which hand is loaded
Opposite-side obliques do the work
Free arm relaxed, not winged out for balance
Slow, deliberate steps
common_errors: Leaning away from the weight
Hiking the loaded-side shoulder up
Walking too fast to feel the core working
contraindications: avoid heavy loading during acute low back flare-up

name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
purpose: The main direct glute strength lift, loading full hip extension harder than squats or hinges can.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a dumbbell across your hips. Plant your feet so your shins are vertical at the top, then drive through your heels until your hips are fully extended and your torso is parallel to the floor. Lower your hips a few inches under control and repeat.
form_cues: Chin tucked, eyes forward over the knees
Ribs down; finish with glutes, not lower back arch
Shins vertical at the top
One-second squeeze at full lockout
common_errors: Hyperextending the lower back instead of finishing with the glutes
Feet too far forward so hamstrings take over, or too close so quads take over
Bouncing reps without a lockout squeeze

name: Banded Lateral Walk
purpose: Strengthens the lateral hip stabilizers that control knee tracking in squats and lunges and support the restricted right hip.
instructions: Place a loop band just above your knees or around your ankles and sit into a quarter-squat athletic stance. Step sideways with one foot, then follow with the other, keeping constant tension on the band. Take 8 to 12 steps one way, then lead with the other leg coming back.
form_cues: Stay low the whole set, no bobbing up and down
Push the knee out into the band on every step
Toes point forward, not out
Controlled trailing step: never let the feet clap together
common_errors: Standing up taller with each step
Letting knees cave inward against the band
Dragging the trailing foot and losing band tension
regressions: Band above knees instead of ankles
Standing band hip abduction in place

name: Front Plank
purpose: Teaches the braced, neutral trunk position that every loaded lift and every punch in this program relies on.
instructions: Set up on your forearms and toes with elbows under shoulders and body in one straight line from head to heels. Squeeze your glutes, tuck your pelvis slightly, and breathe steadily while holding the position. Hold for time without letting the hips sag or pike.
form_cues: Squeeze glutes and quads hard
Tuck the pelvis slightly, ribs toward hips
Push the floor away through the forearms
Breathe: short breaths behind a firm brace
common_errors: Hips sagging into lower back extension
Hips piked high to make the hold easier
Holding the breath for the entire set
Head hanging or craned up

name: Dead Bug
purpose: Trains keeping a flat, braced lower back while the limbs move, the exact skill needed for overhead pressing without arching.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms pointing at the ceiling and hips and knees bent to 90 degrees. Press your lower back gently into the floor, then slowly extend one arm overhead and the opposite leg out until they hover above the floor. Return and switch sides without letting the lower back arch.
form_cues: Lower back stays pressed into the floor the entire time
Exhale fully as the limbs extend
Move slowly, about 3 seconds out
Reach the heel away, do not just drop the leg
common_errors: Lower back arching off the floor as the leg extends
Moving fast and using momentum
Extending same-side arm and leg instead of opposites
progressions: Hold a light band anchored overhead for lat tension
Slower tempo with a pause at full reach

name: Bear Plank
purpose: A harder anti-extension hold that also loads the shoulders and prepares the trunk for crawling and dynamic core work.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Tuck your toes and lift your knees one inch off the floor, keeping your back perfectly flat. Hold for time, breathing steadily, with knees hovering just off the ground.
form_cues: Knees hover one inch, no higher
Back flat enough to balance a cup of water
Push the floor away between the shoulder blades
Ribs down, tailbone slightly tucked
common_errors: Hips rising well above shoulder height
Lower back sagging into extension
Weight shifted back onto the knees instead of spread between hands and toes
contraindications: caution with wrist pain

name: Band Pallof Press
purpose: The core anti-rotation staple, building the trunk stiffness that transfers hip rotation into punches instead of leaking it.
instructions: Anchor a band at chest height and stand sideways to it, holding the band with both hands at your sternum. Press your hands straight out until your arms are extended, resisting the band's pull to twist you toward the anchor. Hold for a beat, return to the chest, and finish the set before facing the other way.
form_cues: Press straight out, dead center of the chest
Hips and shoulders stay square, do not let the band win
Soft knees, glutes on
Exhale as the arms extend
common_errors: Torso rotating toward the anchor as the arms extend
Standing too close so there is no real tension
Shrugging or leaning away instead of bracing

name: Renegade Row
purpose: Combines a row with a moving anti-rotation plank, an efficient two-for-one on time-crunched full-body days.
instructions: Set up in a push-up position gripping two dumbbells, feet wider than hips. Row one dumbbell to your ribs while the rest of your body stays motionless, then lower it and row the other side. Alternate with slow, deliberate reps.
form_cues: Hips stay level, imagine headlights on your hips pointing at the floor
Push hard into the supporting dumbbell
Wide feet for a stable base
Row slow: one second up, one second down
common_errors: Hips rocking side to side with each row
Piking the hips to make the row easier
Yanking the dumbbell instead of pulling smoothly
progressions: Renegade row with push-up between reps
contraindications: caution with wrist pain
use hexagonal dumbbells only; round ones roll

name: Hanging Knee Raise
purpose: Loads trunk flexion from the bar while building the grip and hang tolerance that supports the pull-up goal.
instructions: Hang from the pull-up bar with arms straight and body still. Curl your knees up toward your chest, letting your pelvis tuck under at the top so the abs, not just the hip flexors, do the work. Lower slowly to a dead hang without swinging.
form_cues: Tuck the pelvis at the top, tailbone curls forward
Knees to chest, not just thighs to parallel
Lower for 2 to 3 seconds
Kill the swing between reps
common_errors: Swinging and using momentum
Stopping at hip height so only the hip flexors work
Dropping the legs fast and losing control
regressions: Captain's-chair style knee raise with forearms supported
contraindications: avoid with acute shoulder pain that limits hanging

name: Reverse Crunch
purpose: A floor-based flexion drill that trains the lower abs with posterior pelvic tilt, without neck or lower back strain.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent to 90 degrees and shins parallel to the floor, arms at your sides. Curl your pelvis up so your hips lift a few inches and your knees travel toward your chest. Lower slowly until your tailbone touches down, keeping tension in the abs.
form_cues: Curl the pelvis, do not swing the legs
Exhale as the hips lift
Lower one vertebra at a time
Hands press lightly into the floor, not levering
common_errors: Swinging the legs for momentum instead of curling the spine
Letting the feet drop and the back arch between reps
Pushing hard through the arms to hoist the hips
regressions: Lying knee tuck without the hip lift

name: 90/90 Hip Switch
purpose: Trains active internal and external hip rotation in both hips at once, the cornerstone drill for the right-hip restriction.
instructions: Sit on the floor with one leg bent 90 degrees in front of you and the other bent 90 degrees to the side behind you. Keeping your chest tall, lift both knees and rotate them together to the other side until the legs swap positions. Move slowly with control, pausing in each 90/90 position.
form_cues: Sit as tall as possible, hands off the floor if you can
Knees travel together like windshield wipers
Pause and press the knees gently toward the floor in each position
Let the restricted side move through less range rather than slumping
common_errors: Slumping the torso and rounding the back to fake range
Using hands to drag the body around
Rushing through the transition without controlling the rotation
regressions: Sit on a low box or cushion to raise the hips
contraindications: stay in a pain-free range with the restricted right hip

name: Pigeon Pose
purpose: The end-goal deep external rotation stretch for this block; the right hip works toward it gradually via its regressions.
instructions: From hands and knees, bring one knee forward behind your wrist and angle that shin across your body, extending the other leg straight behind you. Square your hips toward the floor and lower your torso over the front shin as far as comfortable. Breathe slowly and hold, then switch sides.
form_cues: Hips square, do not let the back hip flop open
Support under the front hip with a cushion if it hovers
Front foot flexed to protect the knee
Sink with the exhale, never bounce
common_errors: Rolling onto the outside of the front hip so the stretch disappears
Forcing the front shin parallel when the hip is not ready
Holding the breath and bracing against the stretch
regressions: Pigeon with a cushion under the front hip
progressions: Deeper forward fold over the shin
Front shin closer to parallel with the hips
contraindications: do not force range on the restricted right hip
avoid with acute knee pain in the front leg

name: Figure-4 Supine Stretch
purpose: The pigeon regression prescribed for the restricted right hip: the same stretch with the load and angle fully controllable.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and cross one ankle over the opposite thigh, just above the knee. Reach through and grab behind the supporting thigh, then gently pull it toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the crossed-leg glute. Hold and breathe, easing deeper on each exhale.
form_cues: Head and shoulders relaxed on the floor
Push the crossed knee gently away as you pull the thigh in
Flex the crossed foot
Ease in with breath, back off if the hip pinches
common_errors: Yanking the leg in and holding the breath
Lifting the head and shoulders off the floor, adding neck tension
Letting the crossed knee collapse inward
regressions: Cross the ankle without pulling the thigh
Same stretch seated in a chair
contraindications: stop short of any pinching in the front of the right hip

name: Wall Ankle Dorsiflexion (Knee-to-Wall)
purpose: Restores the ankle dorsiflexion that squat depth and heels-down positions depend on, with a built-in measurable test.
instructions: Face a wall with one foot a few inches away, toes pointing straight at it. Drive your knee forward over your toes to touch the wall while keeping your heel flat on the floor. If it touches easily, move the foot back an inch; work at the farthest distance where the heel still stays down.
form_cues: Heel glued to the floor, that is the whole drill
Knee tracks over the second toe
Push the knee slightly outward, never inward
Note your foot distance to track progress week to week
common_errors: Heel lifting to reach the wall
Knee diving inward toward the big toe
Foot angled out to fake extra range
regressions: Seated ankle rocks with less load
contraindications: avoid pushing through pinching at the front of the ankle

name: Half-Kneeling Weighted Ankle Rock
purpose: Progresses ankle mobility by adding load, producing longer-lasting range gains than unloaded rocking alone.
instructions: Kneel with one foot flat in front of you and rest a kettlebell on top of that knee. Rock forward, driving the knee over the toes as far as the flat heel allows, hold two seconds, and rock back. Keep the movement slow and repeat for reps before switching sides.
form_cues: Heel stays welded to the floor
The weight assists; do not fight it, sink with it
Two-second pause at end range
Knee over the outside of the foot, not collapsing in
common_errors: Heel peeling up under the load
Bouncing quickly instead of pausing at end range
Arch collapsing as the knee drives forward
regressions: No weight, hands on knee only
progressions: Elevate the toes slightly on a small plate
contraindications: avoid pushing through pinching at the front of the ankle

name: Open Book Stretch
purpose: Restores thoracic rotation, which feeds directly into punching mechanics and takes rotational stress off the lower back.
instructions: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent to 90 degrees and both arms extended together in front of your chest. Keeping the knees glued down, sweep the top arm up and across to the other side, letting your chest rotate open toward the ceiling. Follow the moving hand with your eyes, pause, and return.
form_cues: Knees stay stacked and pinned to the floor
Rotate from the rib cage, not by flinging the arm
Eyes follow the hand to bring the neck along
Exhale into the open position and let the chest sink
common_errors: Top knee lifting so rotation comes from the lower back
Moving only the arm while the ribs stay closed
Rushing reps without pausing in the open position
regressions: Place a cushion between the knees
progressions: 2 to 3 breath hold at end range

name: Kneeling Bench T-Spine Extension
purpose: Opens thoracic extension and lat length so overhead pressing comes from the upper back instead of lower-back arch.
instructions: Kneel facing a bench and place your elbows on it about shoulder-width apart, hands together as if praying. Sit your hips back toward your heels while letting your head and chest sink between your arms. Hold the deep position, breathe out slowly, and feel the mid-back and armpits stretch.
form_cues: Hips sit back so the stretch lands in the mid-back, not the shoulders alone
Let the chest melt toward the floor on each exhale
Keep ribs from flaring; the bend comes from the upper back
Elbows stay planted, hands relaxed
common_errors: Arching the lower back instead of the upper back
Elbows sliding wide off the bench
Holding the breath and bracing against the stretch
progressions: Hold a light band or dowel to bias external rotation
contraindications: avoid with acute shoulder impingement

name: Band Shoulder Pass-Through
purpose: A daily-dose shoulder opener that maintains overhead and behind-body range against pressing and desk-posture stiffness.
instructions: Hold a light band in front of your thighs with a grip wide enough that there is gentle tension. Keeping both arms straight, raise the band overhead and continue behind you as far as comfortable, then reverse back to the front. Narrow your grip slightly over time as range improves.
form_cues: Arms stay straight the whole circle
Ribs down; do not arch the lower back to get the band behind you
Move slowly through the sticky point overhead
Even pull on both sides of the band
common_errors: Bending the elbows to sneak the band over
Gripping too narrow too soon and forcing the shoulders
Arching the back as the band passes overhead
regressions: Only go to the overhead position and return
progressions: Prone lift-off (arms overhead, lift a dowel off the floor)
contraindications: avoid with recent shoulder dislocation or instability

name: Wall Slide
purpose: Grooves clean overhead scapular mechanics, teaching the shoulder blades to rotate upward instead of shrugging.
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall, feet a few inches out, and press your lower back, forearms, and hands lightly against it in a goalpost position. Slide your arms up the wall as far as they go without anything peeling off, then slide back down. Move slowly and keep the ribs down throughout.
form_cues: Forearms and wrists stay in contact with the wall
Ribs down; do not let the lower back arch away from the wall
Slide up by rotating the shoulder blades, not shrugging
Stop at the height where contact breaks and work there
common_errors: Arching the lower back to fake more overhead range
Wrists peeling off the wall on the way up
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
regressions: Face-the-wall slide with hands on wall
progressions: Add a light band around the wrists
Wall slide with lift-off at the top
contraindications: avoid with acute shoulder impingement

name: Shadowboxing Rounds
purpose: The program's primary low-impact cardio, building conditioning and boxing skill simultaneously in timed rounds.
instructions: Set a round timer, commonly 3 minutes work with 1 minute rest, and move continuously throwing punch combinations at the air. Stay light on your feet, mixing jabs, crosses, hooks, and defensive movement like slips and footwork. Keep punches crisp but relaxed; speed and rhythm over raw force.
form_cues: Hands return to the chin after every punch
Rotate hips and rear foot into crosses and hooks
Stay on the balls of the feet, knees soft
Exhale sharply with each punch
common_errors: Dropping the hands as fatigue sets in
Arm-punching without hip rotation
Standing flat-footed and square
Fully extending and snapping the elbows on air punches
progressions: Add light hand weights for short blocks
contraindications: stop snapping punches with elbow pain

name: Dumbbell Thruster
purpose: A full-body, low-impact conditioning finisher that spikes heart rate with load instead of jumping.
instructions: Hold two light dumbbells at your shoulders and squat to parallel. Drive up hard and use the momentum from your legs to press the dumbbells overhead in one fluid motion. Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders as you descend into the next squat.
form_cues: One continuous motion: the squat drive powers the press
Full squat depth, full overhead lockout
Heels down through the leg drive
Breathe every rep: inhale down, exhale up
common_errors: Pausing between the squat and the press, losing the leg drive
Cutting squat depth as fatigue builds
Arching the back at the overhead finish
Going too heavy and turning it into slow singles
progressions: EMOM format: fixed reps every minute
contraindications: avoid with acute shoulder impingement
avoid during acute low back flare-up

name: Kettlebell Front Rack Squat
purpose: Primary kettlebell squat pattern; the front rack adds trunk and upper-back demand while staying joint-friendly.
instructions: Clean one or two kettlebells to the rack position, elbows tucked and forearms vertical. Squat down keeping the chest tall and elbows from dropping, then drive back up through the whole foot.
form_cues: Elbows stay connected to the ribs
Sit down between the hips, not back into a hinge
Big breath and brace before each rep
Knees track over toes
common_errors: Elbows flaring and bell tipping forward
Losing upper-back position at the bottom
Heels lifting
contraindications: Caution with acute wrist or elbow pain in the rack position

name: Kettlebell Clean
purpose: Gateway ballistic that loads the hinge and sets up rack-position work (squats, presses, carries).
instructions: Hike the bell back between the legs, snap the hips forward, and guide the bell around the forearm into the rack position rather than flipping it over the wrist. Keep the elbow close to the body throughout.
form_cues: Tame the arc — keep the bell close
Hips power the bell, the arm only steers
Soft catch: no banging the forearm
Wrist stays neutral in the rack
common_errors: Casting the bell out and crashing the forearm
Curling with the arm instead of hinging
Gripping too hard
contraindications: Caution with acute wrist or forearm injury

name: Kettlebell Strict Press
purpose: Main kettlebell overhead press; the offset load builds shoulder stability through a natural pressing arc.
instructions: From the rack position, brace the trunk and press the bell overhead, letting the forearm rotate naturally until the bicep finishes near the ear. Lower under control back to the rack.
form_cues: Squeeze the glutes so the ribs stay down
Press slightly out then up around the face
Lock out with the bell stacked over shoulder and hip
Pull the bell back down actively
common_errors: Leaning back and flaring the ribs
Pressing the bell forward of the centerline
Shrugging into the ear at lockout
contraindications: Avoid with acute shoulder impingement — substitute landmine-angle pressing
Monitor the right shoulder if pressing reproduces any pinch

name: Kettlebell Push Press
purpose: Adds leg drive to the overhead press for heavier loading and light conditioning effect.
instructions: From the rack, dip a few inches by bending the knees with a vertical torso, then drive the legs and finish the press overhead. Control the lowering back to the rack.
form_cues: Short, vertical dip — heels stay down
Legs start it, arm finishes it
Absorb the descent with soft knees
common_errors: Dipping forward onto the toes
Pausing at the bottom of the dip
Turning it into a strict press with a wiggle
contraindications: Avoid with acute shoulder pain

name: Kettlebell Gorilla Row
purpose: Kettlebell-native heavy row from a hinge; anti-rotation demand makes it a strong pull choice without a bench.
instructions: With two bells between your feet, hinge to grab both handles. Keeping the hips square and back flat, row one bell to the hip while pushing down on the other, then alternate.
form_cues: Flat back, chest over the bells
Row to the hip pocket, not the armpit
Hips stay level — no twisting
Push into the grounded bell
common_errors: Rounding the lower back
Rotating the torso to heave the bell
Standing too upright
regressions: Single bell with hand support on a bench
contraindications: Caution with acute low-back pain — use chest-supported rows instead

name: Kettlebell Racked Carry
purpose: Front-rack loaded walk that hammers trunk position and breathing under load; pairs naturally with clean practice.
instructions: Clean one or two bells to the rack position and walk with tall posture and controlled steps for the prescribed time or distance. Breathe behind the brace rather than holding your breath.
form_cues: Ribs down, elbows connected to the body
Walk slow and tall — no waddling
Even breaths behind a firm brace
common_errors: Leaning back against the load
Holding the breath the whole carry
Rushing the steps

name: Turkish Get-Up
purpose: Slow full-body control drill linking floor-to-standing under load; excellent shoulder stability and hip mobility payoff.
instructions: Lying down with the bell pressed over one shoulder, roll to the elbow, then the hand, sweep the leg through to a lunge, and stand — reversing each step on the way down. Eyes on the bell until standing.
form_cues: Bell arm vertical the entire time
Move through each checkpoint, no rushing
Own the sweep — knee lands quietly
Practice empty-handed first when learning
common_errors: Bending the loaded elbow
Skipping the elbow checkpoint
Letting the bell drift forward overhead
contraindications: Avoid loaded overhead position with acute shoulder pain

name: Kettlebell Halo
purpose: Controlled circles around the head that warm up the shoulders and thoracic spine before pressing or get-ups.
instructions: Hold the bell upside down by the horns at chest height. Circle it slowly around your head, keeping it close, then reverse direction. Keep the ribs down and neck relaxed.
form_cues: Tight orbit — bell grazes close to the head
Elbows lead the movement
Ribs stay stacked over the pelvis
common_errors: Arching the low back as the bell passes behind
Rushing the circle
Shrugging the shoulders
contraindications: Skip during acute neck pain

name: Kettlebell Snatch
purpose: High-power ballistic hinge and the classic kettlebell conditioning lift once the swing and clean are owned.
instructions: Hike and snap the hips like a swing; as the bell rises, pull it close and punch the hand through at the top so the bell lands softly on the forearm overhead. Lower by casting the bell back into the next hike.
form_cues: Hips launch it, then the arm guides
Punch through at the top — no flip-flop
Bell finishes stacked over the shoulder
Keep the arc tight to the body
common_errors: Bell crashing on the wrist at the top
Muscling it up with the arm
Overextending the low back at lockout
contraindications: Avoid with any current shoulder symptoms — high demand overhead catch

name: Kettlebell Goblet Reverse Lunge
purpose: Knee-friendly single-leg pattern with goblet counterbalance; pairs well with hip-mobility goals.
instructions: Hold the bell goblet-style at the chest. Step back into a lunge until the back knee hovers just above the floor, then drive through the front foot to stand. Alternate or complete one side at a time.
form_cues: Front shin stays fairly vertical
Torso tall, bell tight to the chest
Control the back knee to a quiet hover
Push the floor away with the front foot
common_errors: Short stride that pitches the torso forward
Slamming the back knee
Letting the front knee cave inward
contraindications: Reduce depth with acute knee pain
